idiom_name: module augmentation / declaration merging for the type side plus a WeakMap (or symbol-keyed property) for the runtime side
implementation_notes: TypeScript cannot attach members to a foreign class at runtime any more than JavaScript can, but the type system has the mirror-image feature: declaration merging. Interface merging lets a second declaration add members to the same interface, and module augmentation - declare module './observable' { interface Observable<T> { map<U>(f: (x: T) => U): Observable<U> } } - teaches the compiler about a capability that is attached elsewhere, with the documented limits that an augmentation may only patch existing declarations and cannot augment a default export. The runtime half is a module-private WeakMap keyed by the instance (typed, non-enumerable, and collected with the subject) or a non-enumerable symbol-keyed property via Object.defineProperty. Expose the capability through a typed accessor that returns T | undefined so callers must handle absence, and keep the augmentation and the attachment in the same module - the compiler believes the augmentation even when the runtime patch is missing.
pitfalls: A module augmentation is a compile-time claim: if the runtime attachment is missing (a different bundle, a tree-shaken module, a prototype patch in another entry point) the call fails with 'x.map is not a function' while type-checking stays green - keep augmentation and attachment in one module and test the absence path.

Augmenting global scope or a third-party declaration you do not control breaks silently when the library adds a member with the same name, and any prototype patch reaches every instance including test doubles; prefer the WeakMap route when the object is not yours.

WeakMap keys must be objects: keying by a string id, a number or a value object makes the entry unreachable, the map is not enumerable so attached state cannot be listed or serialized, and structural typing means a typo in the accessor name compiles as long as the types still line up - name the capability module once and reuse it.
